title: Intimate lives matter: sex, relationships and the Care Act
official: Supporting social workers to include sex and relationship needs in Care Act assessments for people with learning disabilities and for autistic people: a qualitative study
summary:
Background and study aims
An intimate relationship is a close relationship between people who aren't family, and can be romantic, or sexual, or both. This project will explore how social workers can better consider sex and intimate relationships of people with learning disabilities and autistic people during care assessments where they decide what support people need. We will create information and training to help social workers to do this well. Supporting people to have relationships can reduce loneliness, increase happiness, and improve safety. The law says people should get this support if needed. Our team has carried out three research studies with people with learning disabilities and autistic people about relationships, sexuality, and support needs. Although there were differences between the challenges and needs that people with learning disabilities and autistic people had, most people wanted partners for love, companionship, pleasure, and to share their life with. People often felt lonely - they didn’t have the information, support and opportunities they needed to safely meet people and have relationships. We found that the professionals who are there to decide what support people need, and to make sure they get it, rarely ask about sex and relationships and how they can support them.

What does the study involve?
Interviews and focus groups: We will talk to social workers, on their own and in groups, about their experiences of doing care assessments with people with learning disabilities and autistic people. We will ask what would help them feel confident to discuss sex and relationship support needs in assessments.
Workshops: We will hold workshops with people with learning disabilities and autistic people to make checklists and guidance to help social workers to include questions about sex and intimate relationships in needs assessments with 
people with learning disabilities and autistic people.
Training: We will use what social workers tell us to create and run a free online training programme, with help from our advisory group. Afterwards, we will ask social workers if the training helped them talk about sex and relationship needs during adult care assessments.
Good practice case studies: We will find three examples where local councils have provided good sex and relationship support for people with learning disabilities and autistic people and write about what they have done so that other councils can learn from them. 
We will share our resources and findings in different ways: online training, webinars, our websites, magazines for 
social workers, easy-read reports, and accessible summaries.

Who can participate? 
Different people can participate in different parts of the study. 
Interviews and focus groups: social workers who in the last 5 years have done Care Act assessments as part of their role 
Workshops: autistic people and people with learning disabilities
Training and survey: social workers who agree to undertake the survey can attend the training.
Good practice case studies: staff working at identified sites or autistic people and people with learning disabilities who have been supported by those sites

What are the possible benefits and risks of participating?
Benefits: The training and resources developed through this study are intended to improve sex and relationships support for people with learning disabilities and autistic people. Participants will be paid for their time. 
Risks and how they will be reduced:
Time: Participants will need to dedicate some of their time. Meetings will be scheduled at convenient times, and interviews will be conducted online. Participants will be informed about the duration in advance.
Difficult conversations: Some topics, such as sex and relationships, may be uncomfortable to talk about. Participants will be allowed to take breaks and will be informed about their right to withdraw at any time.
Safeguarding: If participants disclose harm, safeguarding procedures will be in place to ensure their safety. Participants will be informed about situations where confidentiality cannot be maintained

Where is the study run from? 
Manchester Metropolitan University in collaboration with Supported Loving (UK)

When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for? 
December 2025 to February 2027

Who is funding the study? 
NIHR Research Programme for Social Care (UK)

Who is the main contact? 
Dr Monique Huysamen, m.huysamen@mmu.ac.uk

interventions.name:
This study involves two work packages. 

Work Package 1:

Interviews and focus groups with social workers. We will conduct 15 interviews and two focus groups with social workers, to a total of 25 social workers involved in this. Data will be analysed using reflexive thematic analysis.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Interview and focus groups (25 participants):
Registered social workers who work in England and for whom undertaking adult Care Act Assessments or Reviews is, or has been, a core part of their role in the last 5 years 

Workshops (20 participants):
Autistic people and people with learning disabilities aged 18+ years and living in England 

Good practice case studies (15 participants):
Staff and autistic people and people with learning disabilities who are connected with the sites of good practice as identified by the research team

Survey (80 participants):
Registered social workers who have attended our training
Exclusion criteria:
Interview and focus groups:
Social workers who have not undertaken Care Act assessments as part of their role in the last five years. 

Workshops:
Autistic people and people with learning disabilities aged under 18 years or those who do not live in England

Good practice case studies: 
People who are not connected with the good practice sites as identified by the research team

Survey:
Registered social workers who have not attended our training
